*****NOTE FROM THE CITY: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the
social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20
(https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf).

Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City Council Meeting of June 29,
2021, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  1. Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for
  consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance
  Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City
  Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk
  at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to
  consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the day of the meeting, and in
  the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence should
  indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to the close of
  the public hearings, will be made part of the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the
  City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

  1. By Telephone-Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members of the public
  can participate in the meeting by telephone to listen and make comments noting the following:

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting; however,
members of the public who wish to orally address the Legislative Body must use the public access options 1 and 2
noted above.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate alternative
formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (42
U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any person who requires
a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe and/or offer public
comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or service by contacting the Office of the City
Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280, FAX at 310-412-5533, One Manchester Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City
Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later
than 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting.

Inglewood, California
  June 29, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  June 29, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
  hour of 2:03 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/ announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.
142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated June
  24, 2021, in the amount of $1,962,599.82 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
  item on the Agendas other than the public hearing.
  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on the Warrants and Bills. Agenda Item Nos. 3,
  Resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Annual Budget, 5, Agreement with All
  American Asphalt to provide construction services for new Centinela Avenue Medians &
  ADA and Street Improvements from La Cienega Boulevard to La Brea Avenue, and 6,
  Agreement with Baker Electric, Inc. to provide construction services for the Traffic
  Signal Safety Improvement Project. She also spoke on Brown Act Violations, specifically
  regarding the time the Special Meeting Agenda was posted.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, commented on Agenda Item Nos. 3, Resolution amending the
  Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Annual Budget, 5, Agreement with All American Asphalt to
  provide construction services for new Centinela Avenue Medians & ADA and Street
  Improvements from La Cienega Boulevard to La Brea Avenue, and 4, Agreement with
  the City of Los Angeles for acceptance of Fiscal Year 2020 Urban Area Security
  Initiative (UASI).
   June 29, 2021

183  PUBLIC HEARING CONTINUED – 2020 URBAN WATER MANAGEMENT
  PLAN. Staff report dated June 29, 2021, was presented to conduct a public hearing to
  receive public comments regarding the City’s 2020 Urban Water Management Plan.

  Mayor Butts order the hearing to be continued to the Council Meeting of July 20, 2021.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Dotson that the Minutes for the City Council Meeting held on January 19, 2021,
  be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  RESOLUTION NO. 21 - 100 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020
  – 2021 ANNUAL BUDGET; PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – ABC BUILDERS.
  Staff report dated June 29, 2021, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution
  amending the Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Annual Budget to cover the expenditures for the
  Park Restroom Improvement Project Phase I – Rogers Park.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Adopt Resolution No. 21-100 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2020-21 ANNUAL BUDGET TO COVER
  THE EXPENDITURES FOR THE PARK RESTROOM IMPROVEMENT
  PROJECT PHASE 1- ROGERS PARK

  and; 2) Approve payment of an invoice submitted by ABC Builders, Inc. for prevailing
  wage adjustments and change orders for the Rogers Park Restroom Project, CB-19-14 in
  the amount of $77,103.83. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 178  AGREEMENT NO. 21-180 APPROVED – CITY OF LOS ANGELES. Staff report
  dated June 29, 2021, was presented recommending approval of an agreement with the
  City of Los Angeles for acceptance of Fiscal Year 2020 Urban Area Security Initiative
  (USAI) grant fund in the amount of $171, 074.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 21-180; and 2) Direct that
  said funds be budgeted for use during Fiscal Year 2021-2022. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AGREEMENT NO. 21-181 APPROVED – ALL AMERICAN ASPHALT. Staff
  report dated June 29, 2021, was presented recommending award of a contract and
  approval of an agreement with All American Asphalt to provide construction services for
  new Centinela Avenue Medians & ADA Improvements and Traffic Signal Modifications
  from La Cienega Boulevard to La Brea Avenue and Street Improvements from La
  Cienega Boulevard to Florence Avenue Project, Fiscal Year 2020-2021, per Bid No. CB-
  21-05.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby award contract and approve Agreement No. 21-181, in
  an amount not to exceed $7,535,813.50 (includes a project contingency of ten percent
  (10%) in the amount of $685,074). The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AGREEMENT NO. 21-182 APPROVED – BAKER ELECTRIC, INC. Staff report
  dated June 29, 2021, was presented recommending award of a contract and approval of

  2
   June 29, 2021

  an agreement with Baker Electric, Inc., to provide construction services for the Traffic
  Signal Safety Improvement Project: La Brea Avenue and Prairie Avenue, per Bid No. CB
  21-09.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby award contract and approve Agreement No. 21-182, in
  an amount not to exceed $1,025,128.50 (includes a project contingency of ten percent
  (10%) in the amount of $98,193.50). The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO AGREEMENT NO. 20-084 APPROVED – TRIFILETTI
  CONSULTING, INC.; RESOLUTION NO. 21-101 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE
  2020-2021 ANNUAL BUDGET. Staff report dated June 29, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of Amendment No. 2 to Agreement No. 20-084 for an additional
  two (2) years (with the option to extend the agreement one (1) additional year) with
  Trifiletti Consulting, Inc., for Program Management Services for the Inglewood Transit
  Connector (ITC) Project.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Amendment No. 2 to Agreement No. 20-
  084 in an amount not to exceed $12,777,531 (total agreement amount not to exceed
  $19,165,601.44); and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 21-101 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2020/2021 ANNUAL BUDGET TO
  INCREASE  FUNDING  PAY  FOR  VARIOUS  PROFESSIONAL
  CONSULTING SERVICES PROVIDED BY TRIFILETTI CONSULTING INC.,
  ASSOCIATED WITH THE INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR PROJECT

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

142  FISCAL YEAR 2019-2020 FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AND SINGLE AUDIT
  FOR CITY OF INGLEWOOD AND THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD HOUSING
  AUTHORITY RECEIVED AND FILED. Staff report dated June 29, 2021, was
  presented presenting the Fiscal Year 2019-2020 Financial Statements and Single Audit
  for the City of Inglewood and the City of Inglewood Housing Authority.

  Mayor/Housing Authority Chairman Butts ordered the Financial Statements and Single
  Audit for the City of Inglewood and the City of Inglewood Housing Authority received
  and filed.

  REPORTS- CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson thanked Randal Curtis and
  Jason Wick of Hollywood Park for their outstanding services to the residents, vendors,
  and City Clerk while attending the Hollywood Park Summer Bash. She also thanked the
  residents who stopped by the City Clerk's table to obtain voting and registration
  information or update their voter registration cards. Additionally, the City Clerk extended
  a heartfelt thank you on behalf of Angela Allen, Deputy City Clerk, to the Council, and
  Kathy Ares for their condolences sent in honor of her Sister, Arlene Parks. Finally, she
  wished everyone a safe and Happy Fourth of July.

142  FISCAL YEAR-2020 FINANCIAL STATEMENTS AND SINGLE AUDIT FOR
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD AND THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD HOUSING
  AUTHORITY REPORT CONTINUED. Staff report dated June 29, 2021, was
  presented presenting the Fiscal Year 2019-2020 Financial Statements and Single Audit
  for the City of Inglewood and the City of Inglewood Housing Authority.

  Luisana Gomez, Accounting Manager, introduced the speaker.

  3
 June 29, 2021

  Brian Grueber, Lance, Soll & Lunghard (LSL), LLP Manager, presented the Fiscal Year
  2019-2020 Financial Statements and Single Audit for the City of Inglewood and the City
  of Inglewood Housing Authority findings.

  APPOINTMENT OF COUNCIL MEMBER FAULK TO THE CALIFORNIA
  CITIES  GAMING  AUTHORITY  JOINT POWERS  AUTHORITY
  REPRESENTATIVE - RATIFIED. It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by
  Council Member Morales that Council Member Faulk be appointed as the representative
  to the California Cities Gaming Authority Joint Powers Authority. The motion was
  ratified and carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on the Warrants and Bills. She also spoke on Brown
  Act Violations, specifically regarding not being able to hear the meeting. Additionally,
  the caller said drones were stalking her and requested a response to her phone calls and
  emails. Lastly, she questioned the Police Report regarding the vandalism of the
  Inglewood Memorial and stated no one knew about the Hollywood Park / SoFi event
  because it wasn't published.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, spoke on problems with the telephone system and suggested
  opening up Community Room A to have residents talk on Agenda Items. He also
  requested updates on the Skill Center, the 9,000 units for Affordable Housing, and an
  Election Schedule for November. Additionally, he asked for a newsletter for District 4.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in the memory of Martha Estrada, a 36-year former employee for the City of
  Inglewood, and Lieutenant Larry Moroso, a retired Culver City Police Officer at the hour
  of 2:39 p.m.

  Approved this ______ day of _______, 2021.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
